function: CNN Bi-LSTM decoder at the receiver recovers the transmitted BPSK bits from the OTFS delay-Doppler matrix Y[m,n] under spot jamming, minimizing BER (p. 4).
system: OTFS link with one transmitter, one receiver and a spot jammer; antennas and carrier frequency not stated; 8x8 block, FFT 1024, BPSK, 150 km/h (pp. 3, 7).
method: CNN (2 conv layers), Bi-LSTM (128 units), 2 fully connected layers, batch normalization; supervised MSE training with soft parameter update, offline training then online use (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Own simulation: BPSK OTFS through FSPL, optionally plus log-normal shadowing (1, 2, 4 dB), with spot jamming and AWGN; no standard channel model or dataset (pp. 6-7).
test_conditions: Training and test conditions not stated separately; BER versus jamming power without shadowing and with std 1, 2, 4 dB, with loss curves per setting (pp. 8-9).
baselines: Hard decoder (non-learned); learned CNN [25], attention CNN [42], Transformer [36], Performer [43] and ResNet-like CNN [30] decoders (Table II, p. 7).
metrics: BER versus jamming power and shadowing std; training loss curves; FLOPs formulas and execution time per model (pp. 8-11).
complexity: FLOPs formulas per architecture (Eqs. 27-36, p. 10) and measured time on an RTX 4080 Ti: 0.004160 s for the proposed decoder (Table V, p. 11).
q1_support: p. 6: "we modeled a communication system incorporating the effects of Free Space Path Loss (FSPL) and shadow fading in the wireless channel"; the shadowing is log-normal (p. 7). Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "It can be observed from the loss values that when the std is set to 4 in Fig. 6(f)"; loss curves are drawn per shadowing setting, which suggests separate training for each. The paper never states training in one condition and testing in another.
q3_support: p. 7: "Hard Decoder: Hard decoders make a clear-cut decision for each bit using a threshold criterion" is the non-learned baseline; "the transformer model is adapted here for OTFS signal demodulation", plus CNN, attention CNN, Performer and ResNet-like decoders, are the learned ones; p. 9: "the proposed method consistently exhibits the lowest BER".
q4_support: p. 11: "Table V presents the execution performance of various models implemented using PyTorch 2 on a GeForce RTX 4080 Ti"; p. 10: "the our decoder combines CNN and RNN components, with the Bi-LSTM having a complexity of" (FLOPs formula, Eq. 36).
q5_support: p. 6: "a random binary sequence is first generated to serve as the data source"; simulated data only. The paper gives no code or data link, no DOI and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 4 although the paper is framed as anti-jamming, a function excluded in Step 1.5: the learned model is a delay-Doppler decoder that recovers bits from Y[m,n] (p. 4: "The task of the decoder is to accurately recover the transmitted symbols from this representation"), so it solves the detection problem of area 4. Reviewer should confirm this reading. The simulated channel is FSPL with optional log-normal shadowing and no multipath delay-Doppler profile is given (p. 6). Table II to V values were read from the page images (pp. 7, 8, 11).
